subject: Routing-induced latency cascade — triage, short-term mitigations & customer note
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@flowmerchant.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Routing-induced latency cascade — triage, short-term mitigations & customer note

Team —

FlowMerchant (high-volume checkout flows) just reported repeated p95/p99 latency spikes starting ~08:45 PDT that correlate with a routing change we rolled last night (policy: .region -> .cost-pref). They’re seeing impact across gen-api and streaming endpoints. Alex is copied for visibility.

Immediate asks:
- SRE/infra: can you confirm whether routing policy re-evaluation is causing a fanout/reactive requeue that exposes KV-cache thrash? Any quick mitigation (temporarily pin routing for this account to prior policy) we can apply?
- Product: if we need to fallback to the smaller quantized variant (q4_0) as an emergency throttle, what’s the expected quality delta and how do we communicate?
- Sales/CS (cc’d Alex): we’ll prepare a short, transparent note. Please confirm any contractual constraints on model changes for FlowMerchant.

I’ve attached a short log extract and a draft customer note (very short) below. I want to get a “we’re working on it” out in the next 30–45 mins while we triage.

Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: routing-sample-logs.txt (snippet), customer-draft-FlowMerchant.md
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Routing-induced latency cascade — triage, short-term mitigations & customer note

Marissa —

Thanks for flagging. Quick notes from initial triage:
- I can reproduce a spike in tail latency around 08:44–08:52 PDT consistent with a route rebalance event. Traces show increased request fanout where our smart router briefly evaluated fallbacks across 3 compatible model variants.
- KV-cache miss rate jumped ~18% for FlowMerchant’s batch keys during the window — my hypothesis is concurrent cold starts + routing scatter caused cache eviction and hot-path row contention.

Short-term mitigations I can push now (need +1 from Karthik to apply account-scoped override):
1) Pin routing policy for FlowMerchant to the previous stable rule (no cost-pref). This is reversible and should reduce fanout immediately.
2) Enable forced prefix caching for their frequently used prompts (reduces KV pressure, low risk).
3) If we still see elevated tail after 10m, toggle fallback to q4_0 variant for non-streaming gen endpoints for FlowMerchant only — quality hit minimal for structured responses, but we should avoid for free-text creative flows.

I’m attaching a 300-line log snippet (routing-sample-logs.txt) with trace ids 6a7b… — will continue collecting heatmap + mem stats.

Ben
Senior SRE
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Routing-induced latency cascade — triage, short-term mitigations & customer note

All —

If the immediate cause is routing fanout + KV miss, the least-risky path is to pin the account routing (Ben’s #1) and push temporary aggressive prefix caching (Ben’s #2). I strongly prefer avoiding model swaps unless the tail persists after those two steps.

Communication guidance for FlowMerchant:
- Keep it brief and non-technical. Focus on impact (we saw intermittent higher response times affecting checkout throughput for a portion of requests) and the concrete mitigation (we’ve pinned routing and are applying caching; we'll monitor and follow up with a detailed timeline + postmortem).
- Offer a short uptime credit or fee protection for the incident window if they ask — run that through finance but it helps de-escalate.

Grace — can you help draft the 2–3 sentence customer note based on Ben’s mitigation timeline? I’ll sign off if it’s conservative.

Aditya
VP, Product
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@flowmerchant.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: DRAFT: FlowMerchant brief (please review)

Alex / FlowMerchant team —

We’re seeing intermittent higher response times for a subset of API calls this morning that impacted some checkout flows between 08:45–09:05 PDT. Our engineers identified a routing policy change that increased internal request fanout and cache misses. We have pinned your account to the previous routing policy and enabled additional caching for your high-volume prefixes; you should see improvement within the next 10–15 minutes.

We’re continuing to monitor the environment and will provide a follow-up with full timeline and any corrective actions. If you experienced lost transactions, please let us know and we’ll prioritize recovery and provide remediation options.

Marissa / Grace (on behalf of Redwood Inference)

--
Suggested quick note additions: uptime credit language (we’ll propose a modest credit for minutes impacted) + a link to a readout once we complete the postmortem.

Attachments: short-timeline.csv

Alex — quick update from the team: we applied an account-scoped routing pin and enabled extra prefix caching at 10:05 PDT; initial telemetry shows p95 improving from ~760ms to ~210ms for the affected endpoints. We will keep monitoring for the next 2 hours and follow up with a full timeline and postmortem link (INF-4821).

If you have any ongoing issues (lost/duplicated requests), reply here and we’ll prioritize. We appreciate the patience — we aim to have a full writeup by end of day tomorrow.

Thanks,
